**Prior Degrees:** PhD, Materials Engineering, 2017

Dr. Gentry Wood currently works at Apollo-Clad Laser Cladding, a Division of Apollo Machine & Welding Ltd, as an R&D engineer. He is leading a federally sponsored research project on applying the results of his Ph.D. thesis to bring additive manufacturing technology to Alberta on a commercial scale. He is a Canadian citizen and UofA graduate of the Materials Engineering undergraduate program in 2012.

Gentry started in the CCWJ in the fall of 2011 working on a Dean's Research Award (DRA) project on nickel tungsten carbide welding consumables. Having completed 4 projects over 4 semesters, now Dr. Wood joined the CCWJ as a full fledged Ph.D. candidate straight from the undergraduate program. While a student, Gentry received 10 scholarships most notably the Petro-Canada Graduate Scholarship, APEGA Ivan Finaly Leadership Award, Neil McEwan Memorial Scholarship in Welding, and GSA Teaching Assistant Award. As a graduate student, he participated in bringing nearly one million dollars of funding to the centre and was able to give back by supervising 18 students as part of the DRA program. 

Gentry has published three first authored peer reviewed papers and two co-authored papers. His most notable publications are "First Order Prediction of Bead Width in Coaxial Laser Cladding" in the Proceeding of Numerical Analysis of Weldability for IIW in 2015 and "Disagreggated Metal and Carbide Catchment Efficiencies in Laser Cladding of Nickel Tungsten Carbide" published in the Welding Journal in 2015. 

#### Project

*Heat and Mass Transfer Aspects of Coaxial Laser Cladding and its Application to Nickel-Tungsten Carbide Overlays*

My thesis aimed to predict the geometry of coatings applied using state of the art laser technology. A model was developed to predict accurately, quickly, and reliable the height and width of a single weld bead based on an engineering understanding of the physics of the process. The model was proven accurate for a wide range of process parameters and has since been applied to different laser types and material systems with great success. This work has served as the foundation of understanding that the sponsor company , Apollo--Clad Laser Cladding, has used to maximize efficiency of their processes and to develop industrial scale additive manufacturing technologies here in Alberta.
